text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in the Danish press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
--- The government wants to slow building activities in order to stop wage increases. Minister of finance Mogen Lykketoft does not want to detail his plans at this point.

--- Phone call prices will fall within the next year as Sweden's Telia and Netcom Systems, are already entering the Danish tele market with considerably lower prices and next year Danish-US company Sonofon is expected to join the price war.

--- Minister of justice, Bjoern Westh, now plans to double penalties for illegal possesion of firearms to almost four years in some cases after the police have found large quantities of firearms at biker locations. The strenghtened penalties will be part of a package of legislative proposals introduced in November.

--- More local authorities are now ready to invite tenders for private care of the elderly, a market worth 20 billion crowns. Danish firms are interested but can expect stiff competition from Sweden where the private care industry is already established.
